points.description: States that the bias-variance dilemma is a problem/principle in supervised learning, arising from the bias of the model and the variance (of the model's output/with respect to the data), i.e. both bias and variance are named as the two error sources.
States that high bias (as worded in the model answer) goes with fitting the training data very well but high variance.
States that low bias goes with reduced variance but the model does not fit the data well; i.e. reducing one increases the other (a trade-off).
States that this dilemma makes generalisation (generalizability) difficult to achieve, using the term generalisation.

rubric.notes: Full marks need all four elements stated explicitly with the terms bias, variance, and generalisation; the trade-off must be stated in both directions. Vague wording such as 'a balance of errors' earns nothing for that point. A wrong statement within a point (e.g. low bias gives high variance with no trade-off, or swapping bias and variance) cancels that point. Note that the model answer's high-bias/low-bias wording is unusual; mark the student's trade-off direction for consistency with the model answer's logic of an inverse relation between bias and variance.
